name: Alabama
sources: Rates (2%/4%/5%; joint brackets doubled): Alabama DOR, https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/faqs/what-is-alabamas-individual-income-tax-rate/

Personal exemptions ($1,500 single/MFS, $3,000 MFJ/head of family) and Schedule A (medical over 4% of AGI, real estate and personal property taxes, mortgage interest, gifts): 2025 Form 40, https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/25f40.pdf

Dependent exemption ($1,000 to AGI $50,000; $500 to $100,000; $300 above) and federal income tax deduction (line 12): 2025 Form 40 booklet, https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/25f40bk.pdf
Standard deduction chart (minimums $2,500 single/MFS/head of family, $5,000 MFJ): https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/25stddeduction40nr.pdf

2025 bills to raise the standard deduction (HB389) and retiree exclusion (HB388) not enacted: https://alabamaretail.org/?p=31163; 2026's only income tax change is an overtime deduction (HB527): https://256today.com/state-rep-lomax-op-ed-alabamas-four-year-record-of-tax-relief/
provisional: All amounts come from 2025 Alabama forms. Alabama's rates, exemptions and standard deduction are set in statute and not indexed, and no 2026 change to them was found.
notes: Alabama lets itemizers also deduct Social Security and Medicare taxes on wages; that is not included, so wage earners' estimates may run a few hundred dollars high.
Uses Alabama's standard deduction for incomes above about $35,500; lower incomes get up to $3,500 more.
Local occupational taxes (such as Birmingham's 1% of wages) are not included.
